title: Properties of Light
seo_title: JSS 2 Intermediate Science: Properties of Light Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: JSS 2 Intermediate Science: You and Energy
standard_text: Light travels in straight lines; reflection and refraction; the colours of the visible spectrum; how we see objects. (summary of the Intermediate Science curriculum, JSS 2, theme: You and Energy)
meta_desc: Free JSS 2 Intermediate Science worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: You and Energy): how light travels, reflection, refraction, colour and the spectrum and how we see. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Angle of incidence = angle of reflection.
body_html:
How to think about it

Light travels in straight lines at about 300,000 km per second. Opaque objects block light and make shadows; transparent materials let light through; translucent materials let some through. We see objects when light from them enters our eyes.

A mirror reflects light: the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection. Light bends (refracts) when it passes from one material to another, such as from air into water. A prism splits white light into the spectrum: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet.

Example

A ray hits a mirror at 40°. What is the angle of reflection?

They are equal.

Answer: 40°

Example

Why does a straw look bent in a glass of water?

Light changes speed.

Answer: refraction

Common mistakes

  • Thinking we see because light leaves our eyes.
  • Thinking white light is one colour.
  • Thinking a red shirt absorbs red light.

faq.q: Why does a red apple look red?
faq.a: It reflects red light and absorbs the other colours.
Raindrops refract and split sunlight into its colours.

items.q: Light travels about 300,000 km every second. How far does it travel in 5 seconds?
Which of these is a light source: a campfire, a cat's eye reflector on a road, a high-visibility jacket or the planet Venus?
c: a cat's eye reflector on a road
items.e: A light source gives out its own light. The others only reflect light.

items.q: A white ball is lit only by green light. What colour does it look?
items.e: Objects reflect their own colour and absorb the others. If their colour is not in the light, they look black.

items.q: A ray of light makes an angle of 70° with the surface of a mirror. What is the angle of incidence (measured from the normal)?
items.e: The normal is at 90° to the mirror, so 90° − 70° = 20°.

items.q: A ray of light hits a plane mirror. The angle between the ray and the mirror surface is 10°. What is the angle of reflection?
items.e: Angles are measured from the normal: 90° − 10° = 80°, and i = r.

items.q: Which describes the image formed by a plane mirror?
c: It is as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.
It is on the surface of the mirror.
It is not changed from left to right.
items.e: A plane mirror image is upright, the same size, laterally inverted, virtual and as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.

items.q: Which describes the image formed by a plane mirror?

items.q: What is the law of reflection?

items.e: This is an example of dispersion.

items.q: A ray of light enters a glass block along the normal. What happens to the light?
c: It slows down and bends towards the normal.
It slows down but does not bend.
It slows down and bends away from the normal.
It speeds up and bends towards the normal.
items.e: Light changes speed when it enters a different medium, so it bends (refracts) unless it travels along the normal.

items.q: A ray of light passes from air into water at an angle. What happens to the light?
c: It speeds up and bends towards the normal.
It slows down and bends away from the normal.
It slows down and bends towards the normal.
It speeds up and bends away from the normal.
items.e: Light changes speed when it enters a different medium, so it bends (refracts) unless it travels along the normal.

items.q: What is refraction?
c: the bending of light as it passes from one material into another
items.e: It changes speed.

items.q: A ray of light passes from water into air at an angle. What happens to the light?
c: It slows down and bends away from the normal.
It speeds up and bends away from the normal.
It slows down but does not bend.
It slows down and bends towards the normal.
items.e: Light changes speed when it enters a different medium, so it bends (refracts) unless it travels along the normal.

items.q: What does the lens in the eye do?

items.q: A sheet of paper does not give a clear image of your face. Which effect of light explains this?

items.q: A smooth, polished metal tray shows a clear image. Which effect of light explains this?

items.q: A straw in a glass of water looks bent. What happens or why?
c: Light refracts as it leaves the water.
It goes straight on without bending.
Light from the straw refracts as it leaves the water.
Different colours refract by different amounts.
items.e: Refraction is the bending of light when it changes speed going into a different material.

items.q: A ray of light enters a glass block along the normal (at 90° to the surface). What happens or why?

items.e: Refraction is the bending of light when it changes speed going into a different material.

items.q: A swimming pool looks shallower than it really is. Which effect of light explains this?
